newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil rallies to higher close, soymeal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil rallies to higher close, soymeal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures rallied late to close higher as prices fell far enough to attract more export demand, traders said.
Soymeal closed mixed with nearbys up on the lack of deliveries posted against the August and new crop down on bearishly construed weather forecasts.

Soyoil had traded lower most of the day but trade sources said when nearbys fell below 22.00 cents per lb and new crop months below 23.00 cents, soyoil was priced to move. USDA weekly export sales data showed exports have been active in recent weeks and more demand was seen cropping up.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soyoil during the week ended August 7 totalled 30,800 tonnes, above expectations for 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes.

But USDA said U.S. net export sales of old crop soymeal during the week ended August 7 totalled 17,400 tonnes, below expectations for 30,000 to 50,000 tonnes. Net export sales of new crop soymeal totalled 15,100 tonnes, below expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
Soymeal ended $2.90 per ton higher to $1.10 lower with August up $2.90 at $258.20. Soyoil closed 0.30 to 0.17 cent per lb higher with December up 0.29 at 22.79 cents.
Weather forecasts weighed on new crop soymeal futures. Forecasts called for widespread rains this weekend with coverage anywhere from 65 to 80 percent this weekend, meteorologists said.

On the day, Tenco Inc was a key buyer of soymeal. Tenco bought 600 lots each December and March, 200 August and 100 September, traders said. Merrill Lynch sold 200 August and E.D. and F. Man International sold 200 December.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 200 October and 400 September while ADM and Central Soya were light sellers, pit sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, against Wednesday's 25,311. Soyoil volume was pegged at 19,000 lots, against Tuesday's 15,831
